Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 110, verses 1–3:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets and the Leader of the God-fearing, and upon his family, his companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement.

In this session we will speak about two surahs of the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The first of them is Surah al-Nasr (The Help).

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes, then glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ [al-Nasr 1–3]. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), without any doubt.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾. Nasr (help) is the empowering of a person over his enemy, such that he is able to overcome him, humiliate him and subdue him. And it, meaning nasr, is the greatest joy that a servant attains in his deeds, because the victor finds great elation, happiness and delight. But if it is with truth, then it is good. It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: «I have been helped with terror for a distance of a month»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (438) and Muslim (521 / 3), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]; meaning, his enemy is terrified of him when there is a distance of a month between them. Terror is the most powerful thing that destroys the enemy, because the one in whose heart terror has taken hold can never stand firm; rather, he will flee like the wind. So His saying: ﴿When the help of Allah comes﴾ means: the help of Allah for you against your enemy.

﴿And the victory﴾ is conjoined to "help", and victory is indeed a form of help, but He joined it to help to draw attention to its importance. This is of the type of conjoining the specific to the general (ʿatf al-khāṣṣ ʿalā al-ʿāmm), like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr 4], meaning, in the Night of Decree. So "the angels" are the angels, and "the Spirit" is Jibril, and He singled him out for mention because of his nobility.

The definite article (al) in His saying ﴿and the victory﴾ is of the mental reference type (al-ʿahd al-dhihnī); that is, the victory that is known and familiar in your minds. It is the conquest of Makkah. The conquest of Makkah took place in the eighth year after the Hijrah, in Ramadan, and its cause was that when the Prophet (ﷺ) made the well-known treaty with the Quraysh at the Battle of al-Hudaybiyah, they broke the covenant. So the Prophet, peace be upon him, campaigned against them, and he set out toward them in secret, and said: «O Allah, conceal our news from them»; and they were not surprised except by his encirclement of them, peace be upon him[[See Dala'il al-Nubuwwah by Abu Isma'il al-Asbahani (1 / 74).]]. He entered Makkah on the twentieth of Ramadan in the year eight after the Hijrah, victorious, triumphant and supported. Finally, "the disbelievers of Quraysh gathered around him at the Ka'bah, and he stood at the door and said: «O assembly of Quraysh, what do you think I will do with you?»" He was the one who, eight years before, had been fleeing from them, and now they were in his grasp and under his control. He said: «What do you think I will do with you?» They said: "Good. A noble brother and the son of a noble brother." He said: «I say to you what Yusuf said to his brothers:» ﴿No reproach upon you this day; may Allah forgive you﴾ [Yusuf 92]«». Then he, peace be upon him, bestowed upon them the favour of pardon, and pardoned them[[Maghazi al-Waqidi (2 / 835), and al-Shifa' by al-Qadi 'Iyad (1 / 110).]].

Allah named this conquest a manifest victory, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest﴾ [al-Fath 1], meaning: clear, great and evident. When it occurred, the Arabs, indeed all people, knew that the final outcome belongs to Muhammad (ﷺ), and that the era of Quraysh and their followers had come to an end. So people began ﴿entering the religion of Allah in multitudes﴾, meaning in groups, after they had previously been entering it individually, and at times a person would enter it only in secret. Now they entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and delegations came to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Madinah from every direction, until the ninth year was called the Year of Delegations. So people kept entering the religion of Allah in multitudes.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: When you see this sign, ﴿then glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness﴾. It was expected that the response would be: give thanks to Allah for this blessing, and praise Allah for it: help and conquest. What is its reward from the servant?

* A student: Thanks.

* The Shaykh: Thanks. That is what is expected. But what is expected has become contrary to what we expect. He said: ﴿then glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness﴾. This is similar to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an to you in stages (23). So be patient for the decision of your Lord﴾ [al-Insan 23–24]. It was expected—﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an to you in stages﴾—that it would be said: "Then give thanks to your Lord for this revelation and fulfil its due," and similar words. But He said: ﴿So be patient for the decision of your Lord﴾, signalling that harm would befall him through conveying this Qur'an and spreading it among the Ummah. ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness﴾. So the response appears to be incongruous with the condition, but when you reflect, you will understand the wisdom. The meaning is that when the help of Allah and the victory come, your term has drawn near, so nothing remains for you except seeking forgiveness and praise, only glorification and praise: ﴿so glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness﴾.

The meaning of ﴿glorify your Lord with His praise﴾ is: glorify Him with glorification joined with praise. Tasbih (glorification) is declaring Allah far above what is unbefitting His majesty, and hamd (praise) is extolling Him for His perfection together with love and exaltation. Combine declaring Him free of imperfection with praise. ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness﴾ means: ask Him for forgiveness. So Allah, Exalted is He, commanded him with two matters: the first is glorification joined with praise, and the second is seeking forgiveness.

Istighfar (seeking forgiveness) is asking for forgiveness, and maghfirah (forgiveness) is Allah, Exalted is He, covering over His servant's sins, erasing them and overlooking them. This is the ultimate goal the servant seeks, because the servant is a dhanub, that is, one who commits many sins, and needs forgiveness. If Allah does not envelop him with His mercy, he is destroyed. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: «None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds». They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?!" He said: «Not even I, unless Allah envelops me with His mercy»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5673) and Muslim (2816 / 72), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. O Allah, envelop us with Your mercy. No one at all enters Paradise by his deeds, because if you wanted to offer this deed in exchange for a single one of the blessings, it would be overwhelmed by that blessing. So how could it be a payment by which you enter Paradise? For this reason one of the knowers of Allah said in a poem of his:

If my gratitude is itself a blessing from Allah, for which I owe thanks in turn, then for every such blessing, gratitude is due again.
How, then, can gratitude be fulfilled except by His grace, even if the days are long and the life is continuous?

﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾. Meaning: He, Mighty and Majestic, has always been Accepting of repentance toward His servants, so when you seek His forgiveness, He will turn to you in repentance. This is the meaning of the surah.

But the surah has a great purpose that only the intelligent perceive. For this reason, when 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) heard that people had criticised him for bringing 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) close to him despite his young age, and not bringing close others like him among the young Muslims, and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) was among the most just of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, he wished to show the people that he had shown no favouritism to Ibn 'Abbas in anything. So one day he gathered the senior Muhajirun and Ansar, and Ibn 'Abbas was with them, and he said to them: "What do you say about this surah: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾?" They explained it according to what appeared only. Then he said: "What do you say, O Ibn 'Abbas?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, this is the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) appointed time (ajal). The meaning is: as if Allah were saying to him: when the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes, then your mission has ended and nothing remains for you except departure. You were not created for this world to enjoy its pleasures and remain in it for long; you were created for a mission that has been completed. This is the appointed time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." 'Umar said: "By Allah, I know of it only what you know."[[al-Bukhari (3627) narrated with its chain from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to bring Ibn 'Abbas close. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said to him: "We have sons like him." He said: "He is from where you know." Then 'Umar asked Ibn 'Abbas about this verse: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾. He said: "It is the appointed time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which he informed him of." He said: "I know of it only what you know."]]. Thus the virtue and distinction of Ibn 'Abbas became clear, and that he possessed intelligence and knowledge of the intent of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that many people lack.

"When this surah was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was the most devoted of people to Allah and the most God-fearing of them, began to say often in his bowing and prostration: «Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You; O Allah, forgive me»[[Muslim (484 / 218), narrated with its chain from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say often before he died: «Glory be to You and praise, I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance». She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what are these words I see you have begun to say?" He said: «A sign has been given to me in my Ummah, and when I see it I say it: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾» to the end of the surah.]]."

So we say: Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affairs, make firm our feet, and help us against the disbelieving people.

Istighfar (seeking forgiveness) is asking for forgiveness, and maghfirah (forgiveness) is Allah, Exalted is He, covering over His servant's sins, erasing them and overlooking them. This is the ultimate goal the servant seeks, because the servant is a dhanub, that is, one who commits many sins, and needs forgiveness. If Allah does not envelop him with His mercy, he is destroyed. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: «None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds». They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?!" He said: «Not even I, unless Allah envelops me with His mercy»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5673) and Muslim (2816 / 72), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. O Allah, envelop us with Your mercy. No one at all enters Paradise by his deeds, because if you wanted to offer this deed in exchange for a single one of the blessings, it would be overwhelmed by that blessing. So how could it be a payment by which you enter Paradise? For this reason one of the knowers of Allah said in a poem of his:

If my gratitude is itself a blessing from Allah, for which I owe thanks in turn, then for every such blessing, gratitude is due again.
How, then, can gratitude be fulfilled except by His grace, even if the days are long and the life is continuous?

﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾. Meaning: He, Mighty and Majestic, has always been Accepting of repentance toward His servants, so when you seek His forgiveness, He will turn to you in repentance. This is the meaning of the surah.

But the surah has a great purpose that only the intelligent perceive. For this reason, when 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) heard that people had criticised him for bringing 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) close to him despite his young age, and not bringing close others like him among the young Muslims, and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) was among the most just of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, he wished to show the people that he had shown no favouritism to Ibn 'Abbas in anything. So one day he gathered the senior Muhajirun and Ansar, and Ibn 'Abbas was with them, and he said to them: "What do you say about this surah: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾?" They explained it according to what appeared only. Then he said: "What do you say, O Ibn 'Abbas?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, this is the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) appointed time (ajal). The meaning is: as if Allah were saying to him: when the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes, then your mission has ended and nothing remains for you except departure. You were not created for this world to enjoy its pleasures and remain in it for long; you were created for a mission that has been completed. This is the appointed time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." 'Umar said: "By Allah, I know of it only what you know."[[al-Bukhari (3627) narrated with its chain from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to bring Ibn 'Abbas close. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said to him: "We have sons like him." He said: "He is from where you know." Then 'Umar asked Ibn 'Abbas about this verse: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾. He said: "It is the appointed time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which he informed him of." He said: "I know of it only what you know."]]. Thus the virtue and distinction of Ibn 'Abbas became clear, and that he possessed intelligence and knowledge of the intent of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that many people lack.

"When this surah was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was the most devoted of people to Allah and the most God-fearing of them, began to say often in his bowing and prostration: «Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You; O Allah, forgive me»[[Muslim (484 / 218), narrated with its chain from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say often before he died: «Glory be to You and praise, I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance». She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what are these words I see you have begun to say?" He said: «A sign has been given to me in my Ummah, and when I see it I say it: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾» to the end of the surah.]]."

So we say: Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affairs, make firm our feet, and help us against the disbelieving people.
